newsitem.title: CHINA: China said to extend grace period on tax change.
newsitem.headline: China said to extend grace period on tax change.

text.p: China has granted a six-month extension for duty-free imports of capital equipment on foreign-invested projects, the U.S.-China Business Council said on Thursday.
The council, an influential trade group, said it had been advised by the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation that the deadline had been extended until June 30.
China abolished duty-free treatment for imports of capital equipment under sweeping tax revisions that were announced in late 1995 and took effect on April 1, 1996.
A grace period had been permitted, allowing duty-free imports until the end of last year.
The extension of the grace period applies only to those projects that had been approved before April 1, however, the council said.
The tax changes were aimed at removing certain privileges granted to foreign-invested companies as Beijing reduced tariff levels on some 5,000 import items.
China has been trimming its average import duties as part of its campaign to comply with requirements to join the World Trade Organisation.
But it has come under pressure from domestic manufacturers who are unhappy with increased competition from imported goods.
Many of these companies argue that if the domestic market is to be opened up to competition from abroad, foreign companies operating in China should no longer be entitled to special treatment.
